vetSays.line: A man, maybe 30s, with a scarred cheek: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
A man, maybe 30s, with a scarred cheek heads out for water. "The well won't fill itself." The pantry won't fill itself.

A man, maybe 30s, with a scarred cheek has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Fireside lesson: A person, maybe 50s, with a nervous tic passes around a big shady tree; at dawn the ground beneath is strewn with fleshy cream flowers. Someone asks a dumb question. Nobody minds. That's how you learn.

A man, maybe 30s, with a scarred cheek was watching. Now they know Hickory Nuts too.
💬 A man, maybe 30s, with a scarred cheek and Anna are hunched over the fire together, voices too low to catch. Company makes the road shorter.

🔥 The fire settles. Henry has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Stripes flowing where no wind blows — I put it down today." "The grass stops moving the way wind moves it. Two amber eyes — then the whole striped avalanche." "It circles, unhurried. It has seen this episode before — and it knows how it ends." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the man in his 30s, with a scarred cheek says "Tell me you didn't go alone." the man in his 30s, with thick glasses mutters "So it bleeds." regDeaths.name: the creek went still, and your arm-hairs stood up
a crow that watches too long and blinks too little
a drumbeat with no drummer, getting closer
stripes flowing where no wind blows
the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still
